newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B share ends lower, seen to hold.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B share ends lower, seen to hold.

text.p: Shenzhen's B shares ended down slightly on Friday but well above the day's lows, with analysts expecting the index to fluctuate in a narrow range early next week on mixed outlook.
The B share index lost 0.45 points or 0.27 percent to 165.08 points. Turnover was HK$150.3 million, down from HK$269.6 million on Thursday.
The A share index ended up 5.22 points or 1.27 percent at 416.17 points on turnover of 8.4 billion yuan, compared with Thursday's 8.94 billion.
Brokers said concerns that Beijing might tighten trading rules exerted pressure on B shares, but investors had confidence in China's strong economic outlook, softening the fall.

"Investors are concerned that the authorities are drafting measures to counter over-speculation, and there is talk that it might abolish some repo contracts," a trader with Central-South Securities said.
The Shanghai Stock Exchange on Friday denied it was considering cancelling two short-term state debt repurchase contracts, which are a major souce of liquidity for China's stock markets.
Brokers said how the market would move next week depended on whether Beijing announced new rules over the weekend.
A series of stories about risk control published in the official media prompted the concerns, brokers said.
"Stocks would fall if the government decides to clamp down, but people are realising that this is a necessary step for the market to become mature," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
Diesel engine producer Changchai Co was the biggest loser, dropping HK$0.26 or 3.27 percent to HK$7.68 on volume of 1.86 million shares.
On the A share market, building materials producer Shenzhen Universe was the best performer, gaining 0.98 yuan or 10 percent limit-up to 10.73 yuan after 11.2 million shares changed hands.
